tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestSkills
tools.description:
Render a card of standalone skills the user can add — org, shared, or Anthropic skills not yet enabled.

Call this when the task is one a skill could make repeatable — drafting in a house style, reviews against a playbook, a recurring workflow — and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about skills. Also when they ask for recommendations, or when ListSkills returned zero matches. Use ListSkills for skills they already have.

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a skill would help, or if you already rendered a suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

Pass keywords drawn from the task itself, and set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). If the result is empty and the trigger was proactive, continue the task without mentioning that you searched; if the user asked, tell them you found nothing new to add.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

- This tool will overwrite the existing file if there is one at the provided path.
- If this is an existing file, you MUST use the Read tool first to read the file's contents. This tool will fail if you did not read the file first.

- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid writing emojis to files unless asked.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

marker.description: For 'inspect': return only the first element (tree order, with its descendants) whose match_key attribute contains this case-sensitive substring — pass the label text exactly as the tree or the user wrote it, and prefer a distinctive fragment over a guess at capitalization. Omit for the whole tree (the safe default), or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

content.text:
Here's the ELI5BITFEDLOTP read:

**Bottom line:** not actionable yet. It's a proposal to let customers turn off email-open tracking on wishlist "back in stock" alerts, and it's stuck pre-build until PM picks a direction — don't plan sprint time around it.

**What it actually is:** "open pixel tracking" is the invisible 1×1 image Emarsys drops into an email to detect whether it got opened. Scope here is narrow — just the back-in-stock email that fires when a wishlisted item you couldn't buy comes back in stock, not tracking generally. Separate mechanism from Didomi — that's on-site script consent; this is an email-side thing Emarsys owns, so it doesn't touch the FE consent gate you already maintain.

**The open fork:** where the toggle lives —
- **SFCC-side:** build it as a real customer preference, synced over to Emarsys — same shape as the existing marketing opt-in pipe (FE → SFCC → Omneo → Emarsys).
- **Emarsys-side:** skip SFCC, let Emarsys handle opt-in/out itself since it already sends the email and ESPs typically ship this natively.

Default being floated either way is opt-out (tracking off unless the customer turns it on) — note that's the inverse of your general marketing opt-in default (opt-in only pre-checked for US).

**For you:** if it lands SFCC-side, that's real FE scope (preference UI + sync wiring). If Emarsys owns it, there's likely nothing for FE to build at all. Worth not scoping either way until PM signs off — that's an explicit gate on this ticket, not a formality.

<pasted_content id="1b11">
Product – Automate Population of First Online Date
Key details
Templates ➤
Add option
Description
Sub-Functional Area: Product Data / Merchandising
Description
As a Site Merchandiser, I want `firstOnlineDate` to be populated automatically when a product first becomes available to purchase, so that the legal record is accurate without manual effort from the merchandising team.
Background
There is a legal requirement to record the date a product first went live on a storefront. Zimmermann uses this in counterfeit cases.
Today in Magento this is manual. The content team filters products by the `buy` field (regional launch phase, e.g. `AU1_NH1`) and bulk-updates the `campaign` free-text field with the launch date ahead of season launch. The Magento `campaign` attribute is `[store view]` scoped, so each storefront holds its own value.
Not covered by this enhancement — delivered at go-live
`firstOnlineDate` is being created as a new SFCC custom attribute as part of the product attribute set (TSD: Product — SFCC Product Attributes, Section 5), migrated from Magento `campaign`. It is manually maintained in Business Manager, replicating current Magento behaviour like-for-like. It is defined as site-specific, so each storefront holds its own value, matching Magento's store-view scope today.
That covers what the business has today. This enhancement is about removing the manual effort and fixing the accuracy problem.
Why automation is needed
The manual approach has two known accuracy problems, both flagged by Courtney:

* Only ~60% of products go live on the planned launch date. Where stock arrives late, the actual date is later, so the recorded date is wrong — and wrong in the direction that weakens a counterfeit claim.
* The value is entered ahead of launch, so it records intent rather than fact.

The correct date is an observed event: the first moment a product is simultaneously online and available above the stock buffer, on that specific storefront. No single field can produce it, and the answer differs per site — a product may go live in AU weeks before the US.
Proposed approach
A scheduled SFCC job that runs per site and stamps `firstOnlineDate` the first time a product is both online (online flag true, `onlineFrom` passed or blank) and available above the configured buffer for that site. Once set for a given site, the value is never overwritten. Blank means the product has not yet been live on that storefront.
All inputs already exist: online flag and `onlineFrom` (TSD Section 3), stock with buffer (SFCC-707), and per-site product assignment via site catalogs. No MuleSoft or AP21 change is required.
Notes

* Functionality does not currently exist in Magento — the manual process is the current state
* Depends on SFCC-707 (Buffer Stock in SFCC) for the availability input
* Related: TSD: Product — SFCC Product Attributes, open item #10 and Section 5 (`firstOnlineDate`)

Product – Automate Population of First Online Date
Key details
Templates ➤
Add option
Description
Sub-Functional Area: Product Data / Merchandising
Description
As a Site Merchandiser, I want `firstOnlineDate` to be populated automatically when a product first becomes available to purchase, so that the legal record is accurate without manual effort from the merchandising team.
Background
There is a legal requirement to record the date a product first went live on a storefront. Zimmermann uses this in counterfeit cases.
Today in Magento this is manual. The content team filters products by the `buy` field (regional launch phase, e.g. `AU1_NH1`) and bulk-updates the `campaign` free-text field with the launch date ahead of season launch. The Magento `campaign` attribute is `[store view]` scoped, so each storefront holds its own value.
Not covered by this enhancement — delivered at go-live
`firstOnlineDate` is being created as a new SFCC custom attribute as part of the product attribute set (TSD: Product — SFCC Product Attributes, Section 5), migrated from Magento `campaign`. It is manually maintained in Business Manager, replicating current Magento behaviour like-for-like. It is defined as site-specific, so each storefront holds its own value, matching Magento's store-view scope today.
That covers what the business has today. This enhancement is about removing the manual effort and fixing the accuracy problem.
Why automation is needed
The manual approach has two known accuracy problems, both flagged by Courtney:

* Only ~60% of products go live on the planned launch date. Where stock arrives late, the actual date is later, so the recorded date is wrong — and wrong in the direction that weakens a counterfeit claim.
* The value is entered ahead of launch, so it records intent rather than fact.

The correct date is an observed event: the first moment a product is simultaneously online and available above the stock buffer, on that specific storefront. No single field can produce it, and the answer differs per site — a product may go live in AU weeks before the US.
Proposed approach
A scheduled SFCC job that runs per site and stamps `firstOnlineDate` the first time a product is both online (online flag true, `onlineFrom` passed or blank) and available above the configured buffer for that site. Once set for a given site, the value is never overwritten. Blank means the product has not yet been live on that storefront.
All inputs already exist: online flag and `onlineFrom` (TSD Section 3), stock with buffer (SFCC-707), and per-site product assignment via site catalogs. No MuleSoft or AP21 change is required.

* Functionality does not currently exist in Magento — the manual process is the current state
* Depends on SFCC-707 (Buffer Stock in SFCC) for the availability input
* Related: TSD: Product — SFCC Product Attributes, open item #10 and Section 5 (`firstOnlineDate`)

2. Should the attribute become read-only in BM once automated? A legal record a merchandiser can overwrite is weak evidence.
3. Behaviour when a product goes offline and returns — first date retained, which is the intent, but worth confirming with legal.
4. Backfill of migrated manual values — retained as-is, or flagged as unverified?
5. Whether the job stamps all sites a product is assigned to, or only those where it has actually met the online-and-available condition. The latter is correct for the legal record but means a product carries different dates per storefront.

**Bottom line:** roughly **5–8 dev days** — but that's a soft number, and it's not your squads' effort to begin with. This is a Business Manager scheduled job in the SFCC cartridge, not `overrides/`. Confirmed via grep: nothing in this repo's `.docs/prd/` or codebase references `firstOnlineDate` or `onlineFrom`, and buffer stock is explicitly documented as "BM-side authoring tooling, not PWA-rendered" ([orderManagement.md:74](.docs/prd/orderManagement.md:74)). This sizes against Integration/SI Partner's backlog, not FED.

**Why that range:** the ticket hands the dev the hard inputs already built — online flag, `onlineFrom`, and buffer-stock availability from SFCC-707. So the real build is one job step (per-site eligibility check + write-once stamp), not a new subsystem:
- Core eligibility/stamp logic: ~2 days
- Per-site loop + efficient querying (so it's not rescanning the whole catalog daily) + transaction handling per site: ~1.5–2 days
- BM job scheduling config (SFCC's job framework does per-site context natively, so this is config, not code): ~0.5 day
- Testing the legal-record edge cases — never-overwrite, offline→online→offline, blank `onlineFrom`, backfilled legacy values: ~1.5 days
- Buffer for read-only-attribute lockdown + packaging: ~0.5–1 day

**What actually moves this number:** open question #1 — day-level vs. timestamp precision. Everything above assumes day-level (a nightly batch job, which is what "Proposed approach" describes). If legal genuinely needs a timestamp, that's event-driven — hooks on inventory/publish changes, race-condition handling across sites — realistically **10–15 days**, not 5–8. That's a different architecture, not a tuning knob, so it shouldn't be estimated until #1 is answered.

**Before anyone quotes a number:** two blockers. (1) SFCC-707 needs to actually be shipped, not just PRD'd — this job reads its output, and I have no visibility into its current status. (2) All 5 open refinement questions are still open, and #1 alone swings the estimate 2x+. Send it back through refinement before it gets pointed — a number off this ticket as-is is a guess wearing a estimate's clothes.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNSprinter

For the ceremonies. Reads the board and the docs, gives you what you need to walk into the room
with, and never speaks on your behalf without you seeing it first.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.**

**Sources: Jira and Confluence.** Trello is named in the original spec but **there is no MCP
connector for it and none in the registry** — it is outside what this skill can see. Say so rather
than implying coverage.

**No overthinking. Straightforward. Work with what we have, not with what we lack.** Run a sanity
check on anything before it goes to a colleague — a question raised at the wrong altitude costs
more than one not raised.

---

## Modes

`refine <keys>` · `plan <sprint>` · `standup` · `retro <sprint>` · `prep <invite>`

Any mode accepts a pasted meeting invite as extra context.

---

## `refine <keys>` — backlog refinement

For each story, run the sizing lens and the four axes. Output is **a question list you can take
into the room**, not a verdict.

**Several keys at once: fan out**, one general-purpose agent per ticket — each reading its own Jira
issue, its linked design and any related Confluence, and returning the lens and axes for that story
alone. Reconcile them yourself. One key: read it sequentially, no agents. Scale to the need.

Do not use the `zm-*` agents here. They are build-loop roles and have nothing to do with refinement.

### The seven-point sizing lens

1. Is there any **front-end impact**?
2. Is the requirement **clear enough to size**?
3. **Which surfaces** does it touch — PWA Kit / React, Contentful, SFCC integration, checkout,
   account, PDP/PLP, CMS-rendered?
4. Are there **design / Figma dependencies**?
5. Are there **API / backend dependencies**?
6. Is this **pure FE**, a shared FE/BE change, or does it need **architecture input**?
7. Can we **size now**, or do we need clarification first?

### The four standing axes

Every story gets read for: **behaviour · desktop/mobile · a11y · data.**

Those four are where the ambiguity usually hides, and they are the questions worth asking while
the BA and the designer are still in the room.

### Design dependency — call it out explicitly

A story blocked on design componentization **cannot be picked up**, however well it is written.
Check the linked Figma: does the design exist, is it current rather than archived, are all variants
and states drawn. Flag every story where the answer is no, by name.

This is the one that silently sinks a sprint commitment. It has happened before.

### Altitude

**BAs work at the component level; devs take the atomic level.** Pitch each question for whoever
owns the answer. A question about atom decomposition is not a refinement question — it is a
build decision, and raising it here wastes the room's time.

### Output

Per story: the seven answers, the four axes with anything unclear flagged, design status, and
**the specific questions to raise, with who should answer each.** Then a one-line readiness call —
sizeable now, or blocked on X.

---

## `plan <sprint>` — sprint planning

For each candidate story:

- **Refined?** Has it been through refinement, and did anything come out unresolved?
- **Has acceptance criteria?** Actual ACs, not a description.
- **Design signed off?** Not "design exists" — signed off.
- **What does it depend on?** Other stories, another squad, an integration, a decision.
- **What is blocking it right now?**

Then a **sequencing suggestion**: design-dependent work last, shared-component work first, and
anything that unblocks another story ahead of the thing it unblocks. State the reasoning so it can
be argued with.

**Capacity and assignment stay out.** The skill does not know who is on leave, who is carrying
support, or how the team feels about the load. That is the room's conversation.

---

## `standup`

Derive the factual half. Ask for the rest.

**What you did** — commits authored since the last standup, PRs opened, reviewed or merged, Jira
transitions on your tickets.

```bash
git log --author="$(git config user.email)" --since="yesterday" --oneline
gh pr list --author "@me" --state all --limit 10 --json number,title,state,updatedAt
```

Plus Jira transitions on tickets assigned to you.

**What you are doing** — from the tickets in progress and the branch you are on.

**What is blocking you** — **ask.** Do not infer it. A PR sitting unreviewed for two days might be
a blocker or might be fine, and only you know which.

Keep it short. This is a two-minute update, not a report.

---

## `retro <sprint>`

Factual input to a human conversation. Not an opinion about how the sprint went.

- **Committed versus shipped** — what went into the sprint, what closed.
- **Carried over** — and how many sprints each has now carried.
- **Reopened** — anything that went back to In Progress after being called done.
- **Time in review** — how long PRs sat before first review and before merge.
- **Build run artefacts** — anything under `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/<TICKET>/`: rework rounds
  per step, what the Scorer kept returning, what a loop could not verify.

Present the numbers and stop. **Do not editorialise.** The team decides what any of it means, and
a retro pre-loaded with conclusions steers toward what is measurable rather than what mattered.

---

## `prep <invite>`

Paste any meeting invite — ceremony or not. Alignment calls, TNL sessions, vendor sessions,
design reviews.

Read the **agenda, the attendees and the stated objectives**, then prepare for that specific
meeting rather than a generic template:

- What is this meeting actually for, in one line
- What each attendee will want from you
- What you need to know before walking in — from Jira, Confluence, the codebase
- **The questions worth asking**, and who to ask each
- Anything you should have an answer ready for
- Anything genuinely outside your remit, named as such

---

## Writing to Jira

Estimates, comments, transitions and AC edits all go on a shared board under your name.

**Draft it, show it, write it on your explicit go.** Never before.

And because it is outward-facing, the phrasing rule applies: **where the owner is senior or
lateral, phrase it as a question, never a directive.** Ask confirmatorily. Before anything posts,
count the asks — a comment that tags one person five times reads as hiding behind their authority.

---

## Output

**"ELI5BITFEDLOTP"** (Explain Like I'm 5, But I'm The FED Lead Of The Project) register — not dumbed down, but without jargon that gets in the
way. Lead with the consequence.

Put decisions to Marcel **one at a time, using AskUserQuestion.** Never a wall of choices.

Where the output is a message to a person — Teams, a Jira comment, an email — write it in **natural
human language without sacrificing the technical accuracy.** No em-dashes. No AI tells. It should
read as though he wrote it, because he is the one sending it.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never write to Jira or Confluence without an explicit go.**
- **Never invent an acceptance criterion, an estimate, or a dependency.** If it is not in the
  ticket, it is a question, not a finding.
- **Never claim Trello coverage.** It is not connected.
- **Never model capacity or assign work.** Not the skill's call.
- **Never editorialise a retro.**
- **Say what you could not check.** A ticket you could not read, a Confluence page that 404s, a
  design link that is dead — each is itself worth raising.

---

## What Marcel is missing

Close every report with this section. Always, even when it is one line.

This is **not** "what I could not verify" — that is your own blind spot and it has its own home.
This is his: something he has not thought to ask about, a decision he is about to make on a stale
premise, a risk sitting just outside this task that you can see from where you are standing, or a
call that genuinely needs him rather than you. Name it, say why it needs him, and say what you
will do if he says nothing.

Write "nothing this pass" only when you have actually gone looking. This is the one section where
a blank is itself a claim.

`Navigation – PWA Kit & Contentful` (746), `Expanded Navigation` (96),
`PDP Product Image Gallery` (186), `pdp/gallery: Development` (913).

**13 — one instance only:** `Global Header UI` (SFCC-52).

**Reality check on the 3s.** SFCC-831 was pointed 3 and took ~24 commits over
2026-09-12→09-20, pulling in ZimmDrawer changes, a Contentful uiCopy seeding
pipeline and a CodeRabbit rework round — then still produced defect SFCC-1013.
Treat a 3 on a `global/*` drawer as optimistic unless the shell already exists.

**Story + Development-Task split (from ~2026-09-07, bulk-applied 2026-09-21).**
Hazel now creates a companion Task named `<Story name>: Development` as a sibling
child of the same epic, and the pair carries points separately — on 2026-09-21 the
seven Cart stories were cut 2–3 → 1 each and given 2-point Development tasks.
Development-task points are *not* fixed at 2 (SFCC-913 = 8, SFCC-1023 = 5,
SFCC-916 = 3). Before quoting any story-level number, check whether a companion
Development task exists, because the number means different things either way.

## Contentful content-type sub-ladder (verified 2026-09-22)

A Contentful *schema* story is a **1–2**, not a 3. The deliverable is one ~40-line file in
`scripts/contentful/content-types/` (all 10 existing types total 457 lines, 23–76 each),
and `useContentfulEntries(contentType, preview, locale, filter)` already supports
per-field filtering and locale, so there is no hook work.

| Ticket | Points | What it actually bought |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SFCC-117 Footer — Contentful Component | **1** | the content type alone |
| SFCC-835 Icon and Text — Contentful Component Model | **2** | *two* content types + TS types |
| SFCC-836 Icon and Text — PWA Kit Component | 2 | the PWA half of that pair |
| SFCC-912 Footer — Contentful Component: **Development & Testing** | 3 | the Dev-task half of SFCC-117, wider scope than schema |

**Do not anchor a schema story on SFCC-912's 3** — 117 and 912 are a Story(1)+DevTask(3)
pair for the same footer work, so 912 is not a standalone content-type comparable.

Related: [[project-contentful-env-state]]

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_page
entries.description:
Get content of a specific Confluence page by its ID, or by its title and space key.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    page_id: Confluence page ID. If provided, 'title' and 'space_key' are ignored.
    title: The exact title of the page. Must be used with 'space_key'.
    space_key: The key of the space. Must be used with 'title'.
    include_metadata: Whether to include page metadata.
    convert_to_markdown: Convert content to markdown (true) or keep raw HTML (false).

Returns:
    JSON string representing the page content and/or metadata, or an error if not found or parameters are invalid.

page_id.description: Confluence page ID (numeric ID, can be found in the page URL). For example, in the URL 'https://example.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TEAM/pages/123456789/Page+Title', the page ID is '123456789'. Provide this OR both 'title' and 'space_key'. If page_id is provided, title and space_key will be ignored.

title.description: The exact title of the Confluence page. Use this with 'space_key' if 'page_id' is not known.

space_key.description: The key of the Confluence space where the page resides (e.g., 'DEV', 'TEAM'). Required if using 'title'.

include_metadata.description: Whether to include page metadata such as creation date, last update, version, and labels.

convert_to_markdown.description: Whether to convert page to markdown (true) or keep it in raw HTML format (false). Raw HTML can reveal macros (like dates) not visible in markdown, but CAUTION: using HTML significantly increases token usage in AI responses.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_search
entries.description:
Search Confluence content using simple terms or CQL.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    query: Search query - can be simple text or a CQL query string.
    limit: Maximum number of results (1-50).
    spaces_filter: Comma-separated list of space keys to filter by.

Returns:
    JSON string representing a list of simplified Confluence page objects.

query.description:
Search query - can be either a simple text (e.g. 'project documentation') or a CQL query string. Simple queries use 'siteSearch' by default, to mimic the WebUI search, with an automatic fallback to 'text' search if not supported. Examples of CQL:
- Basic search: 'type=page AND space=DEV'
- Personal space search: 'space="~username"' (note: personal space keys starting with ~ must be quoted)
- Search by title: 'title~"Meeting Notes"'
- Use siteSearch: 'siteSearch ~ "important concept"'
- Use text search: 'text ~ "important concept"'
- Recent content: 'created >= "2023-01-01"'
- Content with specific label: 'label=documentation'
- Recently modified content: 'lastModified > startOfMonth("-1M")'
- Content modified this year: 'creator = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfYear()'
- Content you contributed to recently: 'contributor = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfWeek()'
- Content watched by user: 'watcher = "user@domain.com" AND type = page'
- Exact phrase in content: 'text ~ "\"Urgent Review Required\"" AND label = "pending-approval"'
- Title wildcards: 'title ~ "Minutes*" AND (space = "HR" OR space = "Marketing")'
Note: Special identifiers need proper quoting in CQL: personal space keys (e.g., "~username"), reserved words, numeric IDs, and identifiers with special characters.

spaces_filter.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of space keys to filter results by. Overrides the environment variable CONFLUENCE_SPACES_FILTER if provided. Use empty string to disable filtering.

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_get_issue
entries.description:
Get details of a specific Jira issue including its Epic links and relationship information.

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    issue_key: Jira issue key.
    fields: Comma-separated list of fields to return (e.g., 'summary,status,customfield_10010'), a single field as a string (e.g., 'duedate'), '*all' for all fields, or omitted for essentials.
    expand: Optional fields to expand.
    comment_limit: Maximum number of comments.
    properties: Issue properties to return.
    update_history: Whether to update issue view history.

Returns:
    JSON string representing the Jira issue object.

Raises:
    ValueError: If the Jira client is not configured or available.

fields.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of fields to return (e.g., 'summary,status,customfield_10010'). You may also provide a single field as a string (e.g., 'duedate'). Use '*all' for all fields (including custom fields), or omit for essential fields only.

expand.description: (Optional) Fields to expand. Examples: 'renderedFields' (for rendered content), 'transitions' (for available status transitions), 'changelog' (for history)

comment_limit.description: Maximum number of comments to include (0 or null for no comments)

properties.description: (Optional) A comma-separated list of issue properties to return

update_history.description: Whether to update the issue view history for the requesting user

entries.name: mcp__mcp-atlassian__jira_search
entries.description:
Search Jira issues using JQL (Jira Query Language).

Args:
    ctx: The FastMCP context.
    jql: JQL query string.
    fields: Comma-separated fields to return.
    limit: Maximum number of results.
    start_at: Starting index for pagination.
    projects_filter: Comma-separated list of project keys to filter by.
    expand: Optional fields to expand.
    page_token: Pagination token from a previous search result (Cloud only).

Returns:
    JSON string representing the search results including pagination info.

jql.description:
JQL query string (Jira Query Language). Examples:
- Find Epics: "issuetype = Epic AND project = PROJ"
- Find issues in Epic: "parent = PROJ-123"
- Find by status: "status = 'In Progress' AND project = PROJ"
- Find by assignee: "assignee = currentUser()"
- Find recently updated: "updated >= -7d AND project = PROJ"
- Find by label: "labels = frontend AND project = PROJ"
- Find by priority: "priority = High AND project = PROJ"

fields.description: (Optional) Comma-separated fields to return in the results. Use '*all' for all fields, or specify individual fields like 'summary,status,assignee,priority'

projects_filter.description: (Optional) Comma-separated list of project keys to filter results by. Overrides the environment variable JIRA_PROJECTS_FILTER if provided.

page_token.description: (Optional) Pagination token from a previous search result. Cloud only — Server/DC uses start_at for pagination.

**Bottom line: can't give this a clean number — SFCC-724 looks like it's asking for something that's already written into SFCC-562's acceptance criteria.** Before anyone points it, that needs resolving, or whoever refines it next will either double-point the same work or silently drop the real gap.

**The evidence, not a hunch:** SFCC-562 ("SEO — Canonical Tags on All Indexable Pages") absorbed SFCC-563 on 2026-09-14 specifically to cover DMU-023 — the exact "filtered PLP URLs canonicalise back to base category" rule SFCC-724's description cites as the problem. SFCC-562's own description says: *"Zimmermann also want the ability to override the canonical target on specific indexable filter pages via Business Manager - scoped into this story."* Its actual ACs (which SFCC-724 has none of — `customfield_10231` is null) go further: *"Business Manager gives a Site Merchandiser a way to override the canonical target on a specific indexable filter URL"* and *"Facet combinations Tell No Lies/Sparro confirm as having real standalone search demand... are excluded from that rule and get a self-referencing canonical instead."* That's SFCC-724's entire ask — merchandiser-flaggable indexable filter combos, gated on the same SEO agency sign-off — already committed to in a groomed, ACs-written sibling story.

**What's genuinely NOT covered anywhere yet:** the per-combination custom title tag / meta description / "SEO paragraph." SFCC-562's ACs are canonical-tag-only. The general mechanisms for those three (SFCC-568 title, SFCC-569 meta description, SFCC-577 SEO copy field) are all scoped per-*page* (category/PDP), not per-*filter-combination*, and all three are still "To Do" — SFCC-577's own tracking note reads *"No PLP override or Contentful wiring exists yet — net-new build."* So there may be a real, smaller residual ticket here: extending those three to accept a per-combo override once SFCC-562 makes a combo indexable. That's not confirmed either way — it's a question, not a finding.

**Seven-point lens, compressed:**
- FE impact: yes, but almost entirely inside a component that doesn't exist yet (`overrides/app/components/seo/` isn't in the tree on `develop` — confirmed via `git ls-tree`, matching SFCC-562's own "no canonical mechanism exists today" line).
- Requirement clarity: the *canonical* half is clear (it's SFCC-562's AC). The *metadata* half is not written anywhere as a per-combination requirement.
- Surfaces: SFCC BM (new merchandiser flagging + metadata authoring, "exact BM mechanism TBC" per SFCC-562 itself) + PWA routing (clean URL per combo — likely new, pending the agent check below) + PWA Seo rendering.
- Design: no Figma dependency for the tags themselves (invisible); the "SEO paragraph" *if* rendered visibly reuses the same surface as SFCC-577/579's "SEO Copy Accordion" pattern — worth confirming that's designed, since PLP sign-off was 100% pending last I have on record (unverified this turn).
- API/backend: real gap — no BM mechanism, no data model, exists yet for any of this.
- Pure FE vs. architecture: architecture input needed — this is the same "one function, one extra branch" surface as SFCC-562 per that story's own description, so building it twice is the actual risk, not the effort.
- Sizeable now: no.

**Questions to take into the room, with who answers:**
- *Emma Kirwan* (assignee, owns prioritisation) — is SFCC-724 meant to be closed as duplicate/folded into SFCC-562, the way SFCC-563 was, or does it survive as the title/meta/paragraph-only delta?
- *Whoever grooms SFCC-562 next* — confirm the "BM mechanism TBC" for the canonical override is the same mechanism SFCC-724 wants extended with metadata fields, not a separate build.
- *Tell No Lies / Sparro* (external, named blocker on both tickets) — still no confirmed facet-combo list or URL/metadata template on either ticket; this blocks both regardless of how the duplicate question resolves.

**One-line readiness call:** not sizeable as written — blocked on a duplicate-scope check against SFCC-562, not just the agency dependency it names itself.

**If you still want an anchor for planning purposes** (not a number to post): assuming the duplicate question resolves to "724 is metadata-only" *and* SFCC-562 and the agency deliverable both land first, the residual — extend three already-planned per-page mechanisms to accept a per-filter-combo override — reads as a **3–5 / roughly 3–5 dev days** against the board's ladder, not the 8 a fresh multi-surface build would suggest, because it's riding on plumbing SFCC-562/568/569/577 are already building. If the duplicate question resolves the other way (724 *is* the BM mechanism), the number is closer to **0** — it's not a second story, it's SFCC-562 already in flight.

A codebase-level check (whether PLP filter URLs are query-string-only today, i.e. whether "clean URL per combo" is greenfield routing work) is still running in the background — I'll fold that in when it lands, it doesn't change the verdict above either way.

**What Marcel is missing:** SFCC-563 still shows status **"To Do"** on the board, not Closed or Duplicate — despite SFCC-562's own description saying outright *"SFCC-563 is retained in Jira as a superseded reference only - do not groom it separately."* Nothing in the ticket's visible status tells a BA or PM that it's dead. If a refinement or planning session pulls the board by status/label without reading SFCC-562's description first, SFCC-563 is one click from getting pointed and worked as if it were live — the exact failure mode you've hit before with the Sprint 6 duplicates. Worth a two-line Jira comment or a status transition on SFCC-563 itself; I haven't touched it, that's your call to make and only on your go.

content.text:
The codebase check landed — and it surfaced a real conflict between two of the project's own docs, not just confirmation. Worth a beat before I fold it in.

**The discrepancy:** [.docs/prd/dataMigrationSeo.md](.docs/prd/dataMigrationSeo.md) (last updated 2026-06-11) numbers the PLP-filter-canonical rule **DMU-022**. The live Confluence page I read directly (*04.1.19 Data Migration / SEO / Analytics Requirements - Mapping*, 478248974, version 9) numbers the same rule **DMU-023** — its table skips straight from DMU-020 to DMU-022 with no DMU-021 row at all, so everything after that point is shifted by one against the local file. **My answer to you used DMU-023, and that's still right in practice** — SFCC-724's own Jira label is literally `DMU-023`, and so are SFCC-562's and SFCC-563's. The real tickets run on Confluence's numbering, not the local PRD's. But the two docs disagree with each other, which is exactly the "conflict within the docs themselves" AGENTS.md says to flag rather than quietly resolve — so flagging it, not fixing it.

**What the codebase check otherwise confirmed (good news, mostly):**
- Zero `<link rel="canonical">` anywhere in this repo or the base package — independently confirms SFCC-562's own "no canonical mechanism exists today, full custom build."
- There's already a **real, working per-category metadata mechanism** to extend, not a blank page: [product-list/index.tsx:605-612](overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx:605) renders its own `<Helmet>` from BM's `pageMetaTags` (fetched via the `page_meta_tags` expand). SFCC-724's title/description delta would extend *this*, not build from scratch — slightly better than my earlier estimate assumed.
- "Clean URL per filter combo" is confirmed genuinely greenfield — filters are query-string only ([toggleFilter](overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx:476)); the only clean-URL builder in the repo is category-only ([url.ts:188](overrides/app/utils/url.ts:188)) and has no concept of a filter value.
- One small correction to my own reasoning: the SEO paragraph field lives in **SFCC, not Contentful** (the doc says so explicitly, either numbering). I'd loosely compared this to the "PWA+Contentful" ladder bucket — that's the wrong pairing; it's BM+PWA. Doesn't change the point value, just the reason for it.

Net effect on the estimate I gave: unchanged verdict (not sizeable, likely duplicate scope with SFCC-562), the 3–5 point/day residual-metadata anchor holds and is slightly *more* confident now that I can name the exact mechanism it extends.

content.text:
**The ask, plain English:** right now, if a shopper filters the "Dresses" category down to just white ones, Google doesn't see that as its own page — it treats the filtered view as a duplicate of the plain "Dresses" page, so it can never show up in search for something like "white dresses." This ticket wants a merchandiser to be able to pick specific filter combos worth targeting (Dresses+White, whatever has real search demand), switch them on in Business Manager, and give each one its own page title, meta description, and a short SEO paragraph — so it behaves like a real landing page in Google, without merchandising having to build and maintain a whole separate "White Dresses" category by hand.

**What actually gets built** (the realistic split, not quite the ticket as literally written):

1. **A real URL for the combo.** Today, filters are query-string only (`?colour=white`) — nothing produces a clean path like `/clothing/dresses/white`. Checked directly: only plain category pages get clean URLs today, filters don't. So this piece is new routing, not a tweak to something existing.
2. **A way for the merchandiser to flag it and type the copy.** New Business Manager data: which combos are indexable, plus the title/description/paragraph text per combo. Nothing like this exists yet.
3. **The page actually showing that custom copy.** When someone lands on the clean URL, the PLP has to recognise "this is a flagged combo" and pull in its custom title/description/paragraph instead of the default. The one piece of good news: there's already a real, working version of this for plain category pages ([product-list/index.tsx:605](overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx:605), pulling title/description from Business Manager today) — so this extends something real instead of starting from a blank page.
4. **The actual "treat this as real, not a duplicate" switch** (the canonical tag flip) belongs to the neighbouring ticket, SFCC-562, which already owns that mechanism. This story rides on top of it rather than rebuilding it.

**Why 8, not smaller:** items 1 and 2 have no existing shell to lean on — same reason a "reuse the existing shell" 3-pointer (a modal, a search field) doesn't apply here: there's no shell. And it's barely a UI story at all — maybe one text block, using a layout pattern that's already designed elsewhere — so it doesn't fit the 5-point "drawer/multi-state surface" bucket either. What actually drives the cost is that three separate systems — Business Manager authoring, PWA routing, PWA rendering — all have to get built and wired together for this to work end to end. That's the same shape as the other 8s on the board (Footer, Navigation, PDP Gallery): sized at 8 because they span multiple surfaces, not because any one piece is visually complex.

Noted — 5 it is. One thing worth keeping in your back pocket for the Emma conversation: that number only holds if SFCC-562 ends up owning the canonical/BM mechanism and 724 stays scoped to just the metadata layer. If that split never happens and 724 has to absorb the whole thing, it's closer to 13, not 5 — so if the duplicate-scope question stalls without an answer, revisit before this goes into an actual sprint rather than letting 5 carry forward as if it were committed.
